newsitem.title: UK: Closing overseas stock market indices.
newsitem.headline: Closing overseas stock market indices.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Thursday.

LONDON - Britain's leading blue-chip share index ended with modest gains as the market breathed a collective sigh of relief that the Bank of England raised official interest rates by only .25 percentage point, dealers said. The FTSE 100 closed at 4,767.8, up 5.4 points, or 0.11 percent.

FRANKFURT - Germany's DAX index tumbled about 1.6 percent in active market dealings, hurt by the dollar falling more than a pfennig on comments from the Bundesbank that the U.S. currency's correction was now over. The DAX-30 index closed at 3,992.38, down 63.48 points, or 1.57 percent. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index ended at 4,000.65, down 26.32 points, or 0.65 percent.

PARIS - Stocks closed lower but ended above their lows as a higher start on Wall Street helped pull stocks back up somewhat, dealers said. A 1.51 percent overnight fall Wednesday hurt stock prices and prompted investors to take profits. The CAC-40 index closed down 21.47, or 0.73 percent, at 2,929.09.

ZURICH - Stocks ended sharply lower, but dealers said the consolidation after a series of record sessions was welcome rather than disturbing. The Swiss market index closed at 5,885.4, down 91.7 points, or 1.53 percent.

TOKYO - Stocks closed modestly higher, as high-technology stocks were bought following a record winning streak in technology stocks on Wall Street, brokers said. The 225-share Nikkei average closed at 19,754.78, up 57.61 points, or 0.29 percent.

HONG KONG - Stocks finished sharply higher after a rally in the lagging property sector and a rebound in red-chip stocks allowed prices to shrug off early losses. The Hang Seng index closed at 14,839.23, up 135.50 points, or 0.92 percent.

SYDNEY - The stock market almost wiped out all of its earlier losses as bank stocks rebounded when long bond yields fell on hopes of a further rate cut following a weak set of June jobs data. The All Ordinaries index closed at 2,694.4, down 1.7 points, or 0.06 percent.

JOHANNESBURG - Gold stocks basked in the warmth of a much-needed rally as a bullion price firming to around $320 an ounce gave a shot in the arm to the ailing sector, dealers said. The All-Share index closed at 7,337.9, up 38.7 points, or 0.53 percent. The All-Gold index closed at 947.4, up 42.1 points, or 4.65 percent, while the Industrial index closed at 8,798.5, up 39.2 points, or 0.45 percent.
